question:
In a model-validation exercise, two unknown quantities $x$ and $y$ satisfy the primary observations $2x+y=7$ and $x-y=2$. A third observation reports $3x+y=10$. The students first use the two primary observations to obtain the unique values of $x$ and $y$ by the inverse-matrix method. They then check whether the third observation agrees with the solution. Finally, they consider what would happen if the third recorded result were changed from $10$ to $12$.

(a) Form the matrix equation for the two primary observations and calculate its coefficient determinant.

(b) Find the inverse of the coefficient matrix and determine $x$ and $y$.

(c) Verify whether the third observation $3x+y=10$ is consistent with the solution.

(d) Examine the revised observation $3x+y=12$ and state the number of common solutions of all three equations.
explanation:
(a)
The primary observations have the matrix form
$$\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1\\1 & -1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
The coefficient determinant is
$$D=2(-1)-1(1)=-3$$
Since $D\neq0$, the two primary equations have a unique solution.

(b)
The inverse of the coefficient matrix is
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{-3}\begin{bmatrix}-1 & -1\\-1 & 2\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\1 & -2\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1\\1 & -2\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}7\\2\end{bmatrix}$$
$$=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}9\\3\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}3\\1\end{bmatrix}$$
Thus, $x=3$ and $y=1$.

(c)
Substituting the solution in the third observation,
$$3x+y=3(3)+1=10$$
Therefore, the third observation agrees with the primary observations. All three equations are consistent and have the unique common solution $(3,1)$.

(d)
For the revised observation,
$$3x+y=3(3)+1=10\neq12$$
The unique solution of the primary equations does not satisfy the revised observation. Therefore, the complete system is inconsistent and all three equations have no common solution.

options.A:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7\\2\end{bmatrix}$, $D=3$
(b) $(x,y)=(3,1)$
(c) $3x+y=10$ is inconsistent
(d) $3x+y=12$ gives one common solution
options.C:
(a) $D=-3$
(b) $(x,y)=(3,1)$
(c) $3x+y=10$ is consistent
(d) $3x+y=12$ also has the same common solution
options.D:
(a) $\begin{bmatrix}2&1\\1&-1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}7\\2\end{bmatrix}$, $D=-3$
(b) $A^{-1}=\frac13\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\1&-2\end{bmatrix}$ and $(x,y)=(3,1)$
(c) $3x+y=10$ is consistent with the solution
(d) Replacing it by $3x+y=12$ makes the complete system inconsistent, so there is no common solution
